title: Force a partition after repeated ready re-approvals of one work item

outcomes.statement: A work item cannot be re-approved as ready indefinitely: past a fixed number of ready approvals the gate refuses, so a stalled item must be partitioned instead of having its execution window reset again.
outcomes.demo: A work item carrying two prior ready decisions is refused a third with an explicit error naming the count and the remedy, while an item with one prior ready decision is still re-approved normally.

uncertainties.statement: Whether scoping the checkpoint existence test to approval.evidence, the seam originally identified, is the smaller fix.
uncertainties.resolution: It is not, and it was rejected. Checkpoint items are a closed shape — the JSON Schema sets additionalProperties false with exactly elapsed_minutes, status, implementation_complete, evidence, and model.mjs:266 enforces the same four keys — so carrying an approval reference needs a schema change. Worse, elapsed_minutes must be strictly increasing across the whole array, so a second cycle cannot express its own 45-minute checkpoint at all; the sequence rules would have to become per-cycle too. That is five sites plus a schema change. Counting approvals needs neither: the decisions already exist in .nous-feedback.jsonl and are already loaded where approval is validated.

uncertainties.statement: Whether a threshold would retroactively invalidate work items already approved more than once.
uncertainties.resolution: Measured before choosing the threshold: the maximum ready-decision count across every work item in .nous-feedback.jsonl is 2 (CHG-022 and US-043; every other item has 1). Refusing the THIRD ready approval therefore breaks nothing that exists today and lands as a live tripwire rather than a retroactive failure. The threshold is a named constant so it can be tuned without hunting for the comparison.

uncertainties.statement: Whether refusing a third approval could strand an item with no legal path forward.
uncertainties.resolution: It cannot. Partitioning is always available and is the intended remedy: the parent takes a partition_required decision and its children are approved on their own artifacts, each with a fresh count. This is the same route already exercised by US-018, US-056 and US-058 in this project, so the escape path is proven rather than theoretical.
